from: September book, night 12 (A Kind and Wise Mother)
p1: The last part of Proverbs has words King Lemuel’s mother taught him. It ends with a poem about a good, wise mother.
She gets up while it is still dark to make food for her family. She spins soft wool, twisting it into thread for clothes. She helps the poor.
The poem says, “She opens her mouth with wisdom. On her tongue is the law of kindness.”
p2: Her words were wise and kind. “Her children rise up and call her blessed.” They were saying, “We are so thankful for you!” Jesus loved His mother, Mary, and made sure she was cared for.
Moms and grown-ups who care for you are a blessing. Tomorrow, give them a big hug and say thank you.
old: Near the end of Proverbs is a beautiful song about a wonderful woman — a mom who loved her family with all her heart.
She worked hard with happy hands. She made yummy food, cared for her home, and helped people who needed her.
She was kind and wise. When she spoke, gentle and good words came out, and she wasn’t afraid of hard work or new days.
The best part? Her children loved her so much. “Her little ones stand up and call her blessed,” the song says. That means they were so thankful for her!
Heavenly Father gives us loving people — moms, dads, grandmas, grandpas — who work hard to care for us. We can thank them, and love them, and help with our own two hands too.
